item.title: IRGC Navy says two 'violating' oil tankers hit naval mine in Hormuz Strait
item.description:
IRGC Navy says two 'violating' oil tankers hit naval mine in Hormuz Strait

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said that two "offending" oil tankers on the southern and eastern coasts of the Strait of Hormuz suffered explosions. 

"These tankers, believing they were secretly trying to pass through the fake Strait of Hormuz route, were prevented from passing by naval mines, causing a massive explosion and fire," it said in a statement. 

"We warn all crews of ships with navigation and positioning systems turned off, be careful not to let the lies of American officials lead you to the explosion and fire of naval mines," the IRGC added.

item.description:
Saudi-led coalition says it downed four drones over kingdom's Eastern Province

The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura, located in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province.

The coalition's spokesperson Turki al-Maliki indicated that a number of fragments had fallen as a result of the interception, with no casualties reported in the initial assessment.

item.title: Infants hardest hit as meningitis cases continue to rise in Gaza
item.description: Infants are bearing the brunt of a continued rise in meningitis cases in the Gaza Strip, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday, reporting more than 533 cases and four deaths since mid-October, Anadolu reports. WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier told reporters in Geneva that the agency and Gaza’s Health Ministry are closely monitoring the situation, with cases increasing rapidly between mid- and late October and “have continued to rise since.” Children under the age of one account for 71% of cases reported since October, with newborns alone accounting for 13% of all cases, he said. item.title: Iran blacklists 26 tugboats operating in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran blacklisted 26 tugboats operating in the Strait of Hormuz for providing services to vessels using an alternative southern route through the strategic waterway, Anadolu reports. The Gulf Waterway Management Authority, an Iranian body established to regulate vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, announced the measure Tuesday in a statement on the US social media platform X. The authority said the decision followed reports received from individuals living in countries south of Iran, as well as field monitoring that it said showed the tugboats were assisting ships using the alternative southern route through the strait. item.title: Trump administration debates targeting top Iranian leaders to end war: Report
item.description: Trump administration officials are internally debating whether the US military should target senior Iranian leaders to remove hard-liners and bring the nine-month Iran war to an end, NBC News reported Tuesday, Anadolu reports. Citing a US official and a person familiar with the discussions, the report said supporters argue such operations could demonstrate Washington’s ability to locate and kill Iranian leaders at will, giving US President Donald Trump an off-ramp to conclude the war. However, opponents within the administration and military warned that leadership strikes could cause remaining Iranian officials to dig in, damage US credibility in future peace talks and expose American personnel to heightened retaliation. item.title: EU must speak with one voice to press Israel on humanitarian access to Gaza: Commissioner
item.description: The European Union must speak with one voice to press Israel to lift restrictions on humanitarian aid deliveries to Gaza, with no meaningful humanitarian response possible without a change in the Israeli government’s policy, European Commissioner for Equality and Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib said on Tuesday, Anadolu reports. Addressing the European Parliament plenary session in Strasbourg, France, Lahbib said humanitarian supplies and resources were available, but access to the besieged Palestinian territory remained severely restricted. “The world does not lack humanitarian funding or supplies.
